titleDv: ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ ޤާނޫނުއަސާސީއަށް 8 ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This is the 8th amendment to the Constitution. It moves parliamentary (Majlis) elections so they happen together with the presidential election, and fixes the Majlis's five-year term to start on 1 December. As a one-off transition, the current Majlis's term is set to end on 1 December 2028, with the next Majlis election held before then and the new Majlis's first sitting on that date.
whyItMatters: Voters would elect the President and MPs in the same election instead of in separate years, and the current parliament's term would end on 1 December 2028.
keyProvisions: Adds Article 72(r): elections for Majlis members must be held together with the presidential election held under Article 110.
Rewrites Article 79(a): the Majlis term is five years counted from 1 December, and the Majlis dissolves when that period ends.
Adds Article 79(n): when a Majlis term ends, the first sitting of the newly elected Majlis must be held on 1 December.

Transitional rule: the term of the Majlis sitting when this law takes effect ends on 1 December 2028; the next election and all related steps must be completed before that date, and the new Majlis holds its first sitting on 1 December 2028.
The amendment takes effect once passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: All voters, sitting and future MPs, election candidates and the Elections Commission.
